exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
cohort: 245 postpartum women (121 vaginal deliveries, 124 cesarean sections) attending Maternal and Child Clinic within 42 days of delivery in a rural tertiary care hospital in South India
finding: Postpartum depression and other psychiatric disorders, along with poor sleep quality, were found to be more prevalent in women who underwent cesarean section compared to those who had vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Postpartum depression and other psychiatric disorders, along with poor sleep quality, were more common following cesarean section compared to vaginal delivery.
